claim: Apple's Services gross margin (75.4%) exceeds Products gross margin (36.8%) by 38.6 percentage points in FY2025, and the gap has widened over three years (34.3pp in FY2023, 36.7pp in FY2024).
stance_target: earnings decomposed by durability class shows annuity-like Services carries a structurally higher margin than cyclical hardware
scope_conditions: FY2025 (ended 2025-09-27), FY2024, FY2023, Apple Inc. consolidated financials
quoted_support: Products 36.8 | Services 75.4 | Total gross margin percentage 46.9 (2025); Products 37.2 | Services 73.9 | Total gross margin percentage 46.2 (2024); Products 36.5 | Services 70.8 | Total gross margin percentage 44.1 (2023).

claim: Services net sales reached $109,158M in FY2025 (26.2% of total net sales of $416,161M), up from $85,200M (22.2%) in FY2023.
stance_target: growing share of higher-multiple annuity-like Services revenue
numbers: Services net sales $109,158M FY25 / $96,169M FY24 / $85,200M FY23
Total net sales $416,161M FY25 / $391,035M FY24 / $383,285M FY23

claim: Apple does not disclose the App Store commission it retains from third-party app sales as a separate revenue line; commission revenue is embedded net-basis inside the Services net sales figure.
stance_target: audited absence underlying the need to reconstruct App Store commission revenue from court records rather than filings
scope_conditions: Apple Inc. revenue recognition policy, all fiscal years reviewed (FY2023-FY2025)
quoted_support: For third-party applications sold through the App Store, the Company does not obtain control of the product before transferring it to the customer. Therefore, the Company accounts for all third-party application-related sales on a net basis by recognizing in Services net sales only the commission it retains.

claim: Apple's own risk-factor disclosure identifies the Google search-placement licensing arrangement as subject to a September 2, 2025 D.C. District Court remedies order in the DOJ v. Google case, appealable by both DOJ and Google, with a reversal risk that could reinstate DOJ-proposed remedies prohibiting Google from paying Apple for search distribution.
stance_target: Google TAC arrangement is a binary, probability-weighted contingent earnings stream rather than a durable annuity
scope_conditions: as of FY2025 10-K filing (fiscal year ended 2025-09-27); US v. Google search antitrust case, D.C. District Court
quoted_support: On August 5, 2024, Google was found to have violated U.S. antitrust laws. In connection with this finding, on September 2, 2025, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia ('D.C. District Court') ordered certain remedies... A reversal of the order on appeal could result in imposition of certain remedies initially proposed by the DOJ, such as those prohibiting Google from offering the Company commercial terms for search distribution. If implemented, these remedies could materially adversely affect the Company's ability to earn revenue from such licensing arrangements.

claim: The EU Commission fined Apple €500 million in April 2025 for DMA Article 5(4) non-compliance and issued a cease-and-desist order requiring removal of anti-steering restrictions; a separate Article 6(4) investigation could result in fines up to 10% of Apple's annual worldwide net sales.
stance_target: App Store commission revenue is under active, quantifiable legal/regulatory attack in the EU
scope_conditions: European Union, Digital Markets Act enforcement, as of April 2025
quoted_support: On April 23, 2025, the Commission fined the Company €500 million in the Article 5(4) Investigation and issued a cease and desist order requiring the Company to remove technical and commercial restrictions that prevent developers from steering users to alternative distribution channels outside the App Store... If the Commission makes a final determination in the Article 6(4) Investigation that there has been a violation, it can issue a cease and desist order and may impose fines up to 10% of the Company's annual worldwide net sales.
numbers: up to 10% of annual worldwide net sales potential Article 6(4) fine

claim: In the Epic Games litigation, the California District Court found Apple in violation of the 2021 anti-steering injunction on April 30, 2025 and enjoined Apple from imposing any commission or fee on purchases consumers make outside an app, referring Apple for potential criminal contempt proceedings; Apple's Ninth Circuit appeal was argued on an expedited basis in October 2025.
stance_target: App Store commission revenue on out-of-app purchase flows is currently under an enforced court injunction, not merely a pending risk
scope_conditions: United States, Epic Games v. Apple, N.D. California and Ninth Circuit
quoted_support: On April 30, 2025, the California District Court found the Company to be in violation of the 2021 Injunction and enjoined the Company from imposing any commission or any fee on purchases that consumers make outside an app... and referred the Company to the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of California for a determination whether criminal contempt proceedings are appropriate.
time_period: 2021 injunction; April 2025 contempt finding; October 2025 appeal argued

claim: Apple repurchased $89.3 billion of common stock in FY2025 (diluted share count fell to 15,004,697 thousand from 15,408,095 thousand in FY2024, a 2.6% YoY reduction) under a new $100 billion program announced May 2025, after exhausting a $110 billion program from May 2024.
stance_target: buybacks mechanically raise EPS with no revenue growth by shrinking the share-count denominator
quoted_support: On May 2, 2024, the Company announced a program to repurchase up to $110 billion... During 2025, the Company repurchased $89.3 billion of its common stock and paid dividends and dividend equivalents of $15.4 billion.

claim: Apple's vendor non-trade receivables (manufacturing partner exposure) were concentrated among two vendors representing 46% and 23% of the total as of September 27, 2025, both individually exceeding 10%.
stance_target: supply-chain concentration risk, distinct from any customer/counterparty revenue concentration claim
quoted_support: As of September 27, 2025, the Company had two vendors that individually represented 10% or more of total vendor non-trade receivables, which accounted for 46% and 23%.
